items.title: Indiana University research spending tops $1 billion for second year
items.subtitle: Shows the scale of U.S. research funding and opportunities for student researchers.
items.imageQuery: Indiana University campus, research lab, scientists
items.detail: Indiana University just crossed the $1 billion mark in research spending for the second straight year. That massive budget fuels labs, faculty projects, and summer internships, meaning more chances for undergraduates to join cutting‑edge work, earn stipends, and build strong resumes. It also signals that the school is a major player in national science funding, which can attract top professors and graduate programs. Keep an eye on upcoming research fairs and look for faculty who are hiring student assistants—you could get hands‑on experience while the money’s flowing.

items.title: Harvard and Yale miss top‑10 in 2027 U.S. computer‑science rankings
items.subtitle: Signals shifting strengths in tech education for prospective CS majors.
items.imageQuery: Harvard campus, Yale campus, computer science building
items.detail: Harvard and Yale fell out of the top‑10 in the latest U.S. computer‑science rankings for 2027, while other schools surged ahead. This shift reflects changing faculty hires, research output, and industry partnerships, suggesting that prestige isn’t the only factor for a strong CS education. Prospective majors should compare curricula, internship pipelines, and faculty expertise rather than relying solely on brand names. Watch upcoming ranking releases and talk to current students to gauge which programs align with your career goals and learning style.

items.title: South Carolina home to the nation’s best regional university in the South
items.subtitle: A top‑value option for students seeking quality education close to home.
items.imageQuery: South Carolina university, campus quad, students walking
items.detail: South Carolina’s flagship school earned the title of the nation’s best regional university in the South, highlighting its high graduation rates, affordable tuition, and strong student support. For students who want a quality education close to home without the price tag of a flagship university, this school offers solid academic programs and vibrant campus life. Check out scholarship opportunities, transfer pathways, and campus visits to see how it fits your plans, especially if you value value and community connections.

items.title: New CPT rule threatens future of international students at Brandeis
items.subtitle: Changes could limit work‑study options for overseas undergraduates.
items.imageQuery: Brandeis campus, international student, office paperwork
items.detail: A new Curricular Practical Training (CPT) rule at Brandeis could slash the number of hours international undergraduates can work off‑campus, threatening their ability to fund tuition and gain real‑world experience. The change stems from tighter federal oversight of work‑study programs. Affected students should talk to their international office about alternative funding, such as scholarships or on‑campus jobs, and monitor any appeals or policy revisions that might restore more flexibility.

items.title: Visa rule leaves international students uncertain about stay options
items.subtitle: Policy shift creates confusion for thousands of foreign scholars.
items.imageQuery: airport visa desk, international student, passport
items.detail: A recent visa policy tweak has left many international students unsure about how long they can stay in the U.S. after graduation, creating anxiety over career planning and family reunification. The ambiguity stems from shifting rules about post‑completion work permits. Students should stay in close contact with their school’s international services, explore optional practical training (OPT) timelines, and keep an eye on upcoming guidance from immigration authorities to adjust their plans accordingly.

items.title: Blocked visa rule could affect nearly 10,000 international students in Kentucky
items.subtitle: Potential loss of enrollment and tuition revenue for state colleges.
items.imageQuery: Kentucky university, international students, campus sign
items.detail: A proposed visa rule could bar nearly 10,000 international students in Kentucky from staying for the full length of their programs, potentially dropping enrollment and tuition revenue for state colleges. The rule limits the duration of F‑1 visas, which many rely on for multi‑year degrees. Affected students should consult their university’s visa office for possible exemptions, consider transferring to institutions in states with more favorable policies, and follow advocacy updates that may overturn the restriction.

items.title: Federal judge blocks ruling limiting F‑1 visas to four years
items.subtitle: Legal win preserves longer study periods for foreign undergrads.
items.detail: A federal judge has temporarily blocked a ruling that would have capped F‑1 student visas at four years, preserving the ability for foreign undergraduates to complete longer degree programs. This legal win means students can continue their studies without being forced to shorten majors or rush graduation. Keep watching the court case for any appeals, and stay in touch with your school’s international office to ensure your visa paperwork stays current and compliant.

items.title: Wellesley pauses off‑campus work authorization for international students
items.subtitle: Limits earnings and practical experience for overseas scholars.
items.imageQuery: Wellesley College, student with laptop, city street
items.detail: Wellesley College has paused its off‑campus work authorization for international students, meaning they can no longer take paid jobs outside campus while studying. This limits earnings and practical experience, which are crucial for career building. Students should explore on‑campus employment, research assistantships, or unpaid internships that meet visa requirements, and watch for any policy revisions or appeals that might restore off‑campus opportunities.

items.title: Proposed cap on post‑graduation stays could hit Kentucky graduates
items.subtitle: May force STEM grads to leave the U.S. sooner than planned.
items.imageQuery: Kentucky graduation, students with caps, city skyline
items.detail: Lawmakers are considering a cap on how long STEM graduates can stay in the U.S. after finishing school, which could force Kentucky‑trained engineers and scientists to leave earlier than planned. This would affect their ability to gain U.S. work experience and could hurt local tech firms that rely on these graduates. Stay tuned to legislative updates, explore alternative visa routes like H‑1B or O‑1, and discuss contingency plans with your employer or career services.

items.title: Time is up for student‑loan borrowers: 90‑day deadline to change repayment
items.subtitle: Act now to lock in lower rates and avoid higher payments.
items.detail: The 90‑day deadline for student‑loan borrowers to switch repayment plans is fast approaching. If you miss it, you could be stuck with higher monthly payments and miss out on lower interest rates or income‑driven options. Review your loan statements, compare plans like Income‑Based Repayment or Extended Terms, and submit any needed paperwork before the clock runs out. Acting now can save you money and stress over the next decade.
